description: Screenshot of a June 3 tweet by Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey (@jack), shown as retweeted by the account jimio. Dorsey urges followers to download the Signal messaging app, quote-tweeting Vox/Recode reporter Rani Molla, whose tweet says Signal became a top-10 downloaded social app on iOS for the first time per App Annie data, and that downloads last ranked nearly as high on the day of Trump's inauguration.

description: Phone screenshot (viewed inside another phone browser at m.facebook.com) of a Facebook post in the group 'Oregon city chit chat 2.0'. The poster claims she found a man walking on her property carrying matches, marched him off at gunpoint, and made him lie on the road until police arrived, adding he had multiple warrants including assaulting a police officer. Four attached photos/video show a shirtless man in a dark cap lying face-down on asphalt under a hazy smoke-tinted sky, and a police SUV with officers at the roadside. Circulated during the September 2020 Oregon wildfires amid rumors of arsonists.
text: 12:12. m.facebook.com/mess. 3:08. 75%. facebook. Kat Cast > Oregon city chit chat 2.0. 14m. Some of you still think we're not being under attack. I found this individual walking in my property as I was driving in, all he had were some matches in his hand. Walked him out of my property at gunpoint and then when we got to some asphalt ground on the main road made him lay down while the cops arrived. Had my husband been here he would have been dead. He has got multiple warrants one of them being assaulting a police officer. Close.
flags: Poster's claims (trespasser with matches, warrants, arson implication) are unverified; 2020 Oregon wildfire arson rumors were widely debunked by authorities
Poster and detained man are private individuals — poster named in the post as Kat Cast; neither identified here

description: Phone screenshot of a Facebook post whose author claims to have witnessed a 'domestic terrorism attack' behind his house: hearing fireworks, seeing a flash, a house engulfed in flames allegedly fire-bombed from a car on Jennings, and suspicious cars driving the street as his family evacuated. Below the text is a dark nighttime video still showing an orange fire glow through silhouetted trees. Circulated during the September 2020 Oregon wildfires amid arson rumors.
text: 11:44. Justin Weaver. Never in my life did I think I would witness a domestic terrorism attack, especially right behind my house. We heard fireworks, walked out and saw giant flash and then a whole house engulfed in flames. A random car fire bombed it on Jennings and I pray the family got out. Trying to keep my wife and daughter calm while quickly loading what we could to escape was hard. Watching suspicious cars full of people slowly driving up and down the street while trying to load hoping nothing is thrown at us is terrifying. I hope no one has to go through this and whoever's doing this just stop. Do you really want to murder innocent families!? Everyone keep your head on a swivel, watch your street, neighbors and most importantly protect your family and everyone you can. Write a comment... GIF.
places: Jennings (road/avenue, Oregon City area per context)
flags: Author's fire-bombing/domestic-terrorism claim is an unverified eyewitness account; 2020 Oregon wildfire arson rumors were largely debunked by authorities
Poster is a private individual named on the post as Justin Weaver
Location inferred from context, not shown
